title: An Open Window in Spring
description: Look at an open window through its glass, frame, sill, and the breeze coming inside.
cardDescription: Look at an open window through its glass, frame, sill, and the breeze coming inside.
focus: These clues describe visible household parts and simple opening and closing actions.
solvingTip: Start with an everyday action or something you can see through the glass.
words: Glass-covered opening that lets light into a room
One flat piece of glass in a window
Structure surrounding and holding the window
Ledge along the bottom of a window
Small fastener keeping a window closed
Clear hard material in the window
Move the window so air can come in
Mesh barrier helping keep insects out
Light movement of air through an open window
Fabric hanging beside or across a window
Sky object sending daylight through the glass
Brightness entering the room through a window

answerNotes.WINDOW: Some windows open for air, while others remain fixed in place.
answerNotes.PANE: A pane is the glass itself rather than the whole frame.
answerNotes.FRAME: The frame supports the window's glass and opening parts.
answerNotes.SILL: A sill forms the lower ledge rather than a side or top edge.
answerNotes.LATCH: A latch secures the opening part until it is released.

title: Locking the Front Door
description: Find the key, knob, latch, and familiar actions used at the front door.
cardDescription: Find the key, knob, latch, and familiar actions used at the front door.
focus: A key operates a lock. Hinges let the door move, while a knob or handle gives a place to hold it.
solvingTip: Try an action word before the door's smaller parts.
words: Device secured or released with a door key
Small shaped tool used to unlock the front door
Round handle turned when opening many doors
Extra key kept in case the usual one is unavailable
Curved holder where keys may hang inside the house
Movable entrance panel at the front of the house
Fastener that holds the entrance panel shut
Rotate the key or knob with the hand
Move the entrance panel to let someone pass
Shut the entrance panel after coming inside
Joint letting the entrance panel swing
Place reached through one's own front door
Clothing pouch used to carry a house key

answerNotes.LOCK: A lock controls access; it is different from the hinge that lets the door swing.
answerNotes.KEY: A key is matched to a lock rather than being a general-purpose handle.
answerNotes.KNOB: A knob is the hand grip, rather than the lock's key opening.
answerNotes.SPARE: Spare means an additional copy rather than a different kind of lock.
answerNotes.HOOK: A hook provides a storage place for the key ring.

title: Inside an Upholstered Armchair
description: Look beneath an armchair’s soft covering through its padding, frame, and finishing edges.
cardDescription: Look beneath an armchair’s soft covering through its padding, frame, and finishing edges.
focus: Upholstery combines a supporting structure with padding and a cover. The clues distinguish the outer fabric from the webbing and cushioning layers below it.
solvingTip: Use the layer or body location described before choosing a textile term.
words: Padding and covering work applied to furniture
Soft padded support on an armchair's seat or back
Strong bands forming support beneath some chair padding
Raised covered cord finishing an upholstered seam
Soft sheetlike padding layer beneath a furniture cover
Small nail securing fabric or webbing to a furniture frame
Side support for an armchair sitter's forearm
Part of the chair supporting the sitter's weight
Upright support behind a seated person
Rigid structure beneath the armchair's padding
Resilient metal component supporting some upholstered seats
Cloth forming the visible chair covering
Spongy material used for many furniture cushions
Stitched join between pieces of upholstery cloth
Fabric panel hanging below the chair's main upholstered body

answerNotes.UPHOLSTERY: Upholstery includes more than the visible cloth; supporting and cushioning materials contribute to the finished seat.
answerNotes.CUSHION: A cushion contains padding within a cover, while the chair's frame supplies the rigid structure.
answerNotes.WEBBING: Webbing spans the frame in many traditional seats; it differs from the outer decorative fabric.
answerNotes.WELT: A welt defines an edge or seam; the cord is enclosed by a covering strip.
answerNotes.BATTING: Batting smooths or cushions the surface between other stuffing materials and the cover.
answerNotes.TACK: A tack fastens material mechanically rather than bonding it with glue.

title: Dishes in the Kitchen Cupboard
description: Put familiar cups, bowls, and plates onto a kitchen shelf behind the cupboard door.
cardDescription: Put familiar cups, bowls, and plates onto a kitchen shelf behind the cupboard door.
focus: The clues focus on stored dishes and simple cupboard parts rather than woodworking joints.
solvingTip: The shortest dish names provide helpful crossings.
words: Kitchen storage space with shelves behind a door
Flat support holding dishes inside the cupboard
Part pulled to open the cupboard door
Joint allowing the cupboard door to swing
Panel opened to reach the cupboard's shelves
Flat dish stored upright or in a pile
Deep round dish used for soup or cereal
Small handled vessel for a hot drink
Drinking vessel that is often clear
Material used for many kitchen cupboards
Free of dirt, as dishes should be before storage
Put dishes away until they are needed
Move the cupboard door to reach the dishes

answerNotes.CUPBOARD: A cupboard keeps dishes or other household items together.
answerNotes.SHELF: A shelf supports objects rather than covering the front opening.
answerNotes.HANDLE: A handle can be a bar or another graspable shape.
answerNotes.HINGE: Hinges connect the moving door to its supporting frame.
answerNotes.STACK: Stack is an action here rather than the cupboard itself.

title: Looking at a Handwoven Rug
description: Explore a woven floor covering through its thread directions, raised surface, and finished edges.
cardDescription: Explore a woven floor covering through its thread directions, raised surface, and finished edges.
focus: Weaving crosses lengthwise and crosswise strands, while some rugs add a raised pile. A flatwoven surface and a pile surface are different structures rather than just different colors.
solvingTip: Separate the direction of a strand from the texture or edge formed by the finished work.
words: Raised surface made of loops or cut fibers on some rugs
Lengthwise strands held under tension during weaving
Crosswise strand interlaced through a rug's lengthwise threads
Finished lengthwise edge of woven material
Rug construction without an upright pile layer
Tied fastening used to form pile in many rugs
Loose thread ends extending from a rug's boundary
Small bunch of fibers projecting from a textile backing
Sheep-derived fiber used in many woven rugs
Plant fiber used for some rug strands or foundations
Decorative outer band around a rug's design
Frame or machine holding threads for weaving
Reverse side of the rug beneath its visible surface
Single line of repeated weaving or knotting

answerNotes.PILE: Pile describes the raised textile surface; a flatwoven rug does not have the same upright layer.
answerNotes.WARP: Warp forms the supported lengthwise set, while weft passes across it.
answerNotes.WEFT: Weft runs across the warp; the two directions have different names even when the fibers match.
answerNotes.SELVAGE: A selvage forms along the side during weaving, distinct from a cut end finished afterward.
answerNotes.FLATWEAVE: Flatweave describes structure rather than one national style or fiber material.
